index.encoding: bare global kind tokens; contentless positional FTS5; same encoding as ast-index-spike
index.build: once per source digest and grammar at file preparation
index.partitionBehavior: reuse existing corpus entries; no tape export, token construction, or FTS insertion
index.invalidation: changed source or grammar, and removal; unchanged context-only updates and retries reuse postings
index.readers: pooled connections, independent temporary schemas, coherent WAL snapshots
index.storage: owned temporary SQLite file; retained until the last workspace query lease drops
index.fileCounts: SQL file_kind_counts keyed by (fid,code), for file-scoped replacement and deletion

vocabFileFilter.query: SELECT offset FROM inst WHERE term=? AND doc=?
vocabFileFilter.note: Standalone SQLite access-path diagnostic. Rows for the requested file remain identical. It measures the built-in vocabulary table, not full rule performance.

validationLimits.gitGuardReason: git add . is prohibited for agents; test fixtures invoke it
validationLimits.allocatorProbeUnavailable: system-malloc shim does not implement jemalloc arenas.create

diagnostics.bundledSourceObservation: fts5VocabBestIndexMethod accepts term constraints and does not accept doc constraints; file filtering is applied after vocabulary iteration.

limitations: This change retains indexes across workspace revisions and file partitions. It does not persist them across process restarts.
Built-in fts5vocab supports term seeking; SQL doc filters do not seek directly to one file's postings.
Candidate compiler broadening and conservative sibling selection remain.
Measurements use bounded subsets and a shared host, not a full repository performance claim.
The saved Rust reference retains its prior SQLite page-cache compile option; branch comparisons do not isolate storage alone.
